# protoc-gen-clojure

A `protoc` and `buf` codegen plugin that emits Clojure, with first-class support
for **Protobuf Edition 2024**.

Generated code is a `defrecord` per message plus straight-line `->proto` /
`proto->` functions built on `FieldDescriptor`s resolved once at load time — the
shape is known at codegen time, so the representation is too. Services come out
as descriptors ready for a Clojure gRPC runtime.

```clj
;; Generated by protoc-gen-clojure from acme/greeter/greeter.proto. Do not edit.
(ns acme.greeter.greeter
  (:require [clj-grpc.codec :as codec]
            [clj-grpc.runtime :as rt]
            [clj-grpc.runtime.service :as rts]))

(defrecord HelloRequest [name])
(defn HelloRequest->proto ...)
(defn proto->HelloRequest ...)
(def Greeter (rts/service file-descriptor "Greeter"))
```

## Editions

The reason most third-party plugins break on a new edition is a hardcoded
maximum. This one probes instead: it asks the linked `protobuf-java` which
editions it can *actually resolve* by building a trivial descriptor at each
candidate, and advertises the highest that succeeds. Bumping the `protobuf-java`
dependency raises the ceiling on its own.

It also performs no feature resolution of its own. The emitted file embeds the
`FileDescriptorProto` verbatim and lets `protobuf-java` resolve edition features
at load time, so a future edition needs no codegen change at all.

Enum membership is not evidence of support: `protobuf-java` 4.35.1 lists
`EDITION_2026` long before it can resolve it, so that value is probed and
declined rather than advertised.

## Install

Download a binary for your platform from
[Releases](https://github.com/bpalermo/protoc-gen-clojure/releases) and put it on
`PATH`. The **file name matters** — `protoc` discovers plugins as
`protoc-gen-<name>`, and that is what makes `--clojure_out` work:

```sh
VERSION=0.1.0
curl -fsSLo protoc-gen-clojure \
  "https://github.com/bpalermo/protoc-gen-clojure/releases/download/v$VERSION/protoc-gen-clojure_${VERSION}_linux_x86_64"
chmod +x protoc-gen-clojure && mv protoc-gen-clojure /usr/local/bin/
```

On macOS, a binary downloaded from the internet carries a quarantine attribute
and will be killed on first run. Clear it:

```sh
xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /usr/local/bin/protoc-gen-clojure
```

Binaries are unsigned and un-notarized for now.

## Use

### protoc

```sh
protoc --clojure_out=src/gen hello.proto
```

### buf

A `local:` plugin, no registry involved:

```yaml
# buf.gen.yaml
version: v2
plugins:
  - local: protoc-gen-clojure
    out: src/gen
```

Remote execution on the BSR (`buf.build/bpalermo/clojure`) is prepared but not
published — public plugin publishing there is not self-serve. See
`buf.plugin.yaml`.

### Bazel

Consumers need **no Clojure, no JVM and no GraalVM**: the toolchain fetches a
prebuilt native binary for the host platform.

```starlark
# MODULE.bazel
bazel_dep(name = "protoc_gen_clojure", version = "0.1.0")

plugin = use_extension("@protoc_gen_clojure//bazel:extensions.bzl", "toolchains")
use_repo(plugin, "protoc_gen_clojure_toolchains")

register_toolchains("@protoc_gen_clojure_toolchains//:all")
```

```starlark
# BUILD.bazel
load("@protoc_gen_clojure//bazel:defs.bzl", "clojure_proto_library")

clojure_proto_library(
    name = "hello_clj",
    outs = ["example/hello.clj"],
    proto = ":hello_proto",
)
```

A complete, working example is in [`examples/bzlmod`](examples/bzlmod) — which is
also the module BCR runs against on every release.

`clojure_proto_library` is a real Starlark rule rather than a `genrule` for a
specific reason: protoc must be able to resolve every transitive import, and the
only way to give it them is `--descriptor_set_in` with the *transitive* descriptor
sets. Those live on `ProtoInfo`, which a `genrule` cannot reach. (`--proto_path`
is not an alternative: edition 2024's `import option java_features.proto` is
exported in no protobuf filegroup.)

## Options

Comma-separated, as `--clojure_out=key=value,key2=value2:DIR`, or via
`clojure_proto_library`'s `options` attribute:

| option | meaning |
|---|---|
| `ns_prefix=foo` | prefix every generated namespace with `foo.` |
| `keep_source_info=true` | embed `SourceCodeInfo` (comments and spans). Off by default: it dominates the payload and is useless at runtime. |

## Limitations

- **Nested messages** get no record yet (issue #2). The enclosing message still
  round-trips; only the convenience record and conversion functions are missing,
  and the generated file names what was skipped so it is not a silent gap.
- No Windows binaries.
- BSR remote execution is prepared but unpublished.

## Development

Bazel is pinned by `.bazelversion` (9.2.0). It is not incidental: the rules load
`ProtoInfo` from `@protobuf` because Bazel 9 removed it from the Starlark globals,
and `rules_clojure` is a fork carrying Bazel 9 compatibility patches.


```sh
bazel test //...                      # everything, lint included
bazel test //... --test_tag_filters=lint   # just lint: buf, shellcheck, formatting
bazel run //bazel/dev:format          # FIX formatting (buf format, buildifier)
bazel run //test:update_golden        # after an intended codegen change

# The native binary is a Bazel artifact, and this runs it under real protoc and
# buf — both hermetic — in a scratch directory with only the plugin on PATH.
bazel build //src/clj_grpc:protoc_gen_clojure
bazel test  //test:distribution_test

# The same check against an arbitrary binary, e.g. a downloaded release asset:
PLUGIN=/path/to/protoc-gen-clojure bazel run //test:distribution_check
```

Emission is pinned by golden files under `test/golden`. A change to the emitter
shows up as a diff there, and that diff *is* the change — review it.

Lint runs as ordinary Bazel tests, so `bazel test //...` fails on a lint error and
CI needs no separate lint job. `bazel run //bazel/dev:format` fixes what is mechanically
fixable — buf for protos, buildifier for Starlark. Every tool is hermetic and
pinned by `MODULE.bazel`: buf lints with the same 1.72.0 the distribution test
verifies with.

Shell is linted but not formatted. shfmt is only reachable through `@multitool`,
and registering that hub needs a non-dev `use_extension` on a dev-only module,
which makes `@rules_multitool` invisible to consumers and breaks them at module
resolution. shellcheck is unaffected — rules_lint aliases it inside its own repo.

shellcheck is not decoration here: `SC2318` catches exactly the bug this repo
already shipped — `local dir="$1" out="$dir/x"`, where bash expands every word of
a `local` before performing any of its assignments, so the script died under
`set -u`.

Whether the generated code actually *works* — round-trips on the wire, serves
real RPCs, stays byte-identical to protoc's Java backend — is asserted by the
runtime library the generated code requires, which owns those tests. That is what
lets this module depend on nothing but `protobuf-java`.

The native binary is built by `//bazel:native_image.bzl`, a small rule of our own
rather than rules_graalvm's — whose rule crashes Bazel on macOS by setting
`SDKROOT` twice (once itself via `apple_support`, once via Bazel's own Xcode env
provider). The rule is honest about its one compromise: the action is local and
unsandboxed with the ambient environment, because native-image shells out to the
platform linker.

Windows binaries are not built yet.
